compiled_state.title: [merge-to-main]: re-run/--resume after PR1 CI failure -> 'non-draft PR already exists', branch wedged
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 42562899446ee7c15defab0ef657aabb198f8425
* **Scripts:** plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (via .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh), wait-for-pr.sh
* **Workflow:** dso.workflow=ci-pr, two-channel staged model (worktree -> staged-* [PR1] -> main [PR2])

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker (merge automation, autonomous discovery)

#### Expected Behavior

If merge-to-main creates PR1 (worktree -> staged-*) and PR1's CI then fails on a fixable check, the operator should be able to push a fix and re-run (or --resume) merge-to-main to: reuse the existing open PR1, wait for its re-run checks, merge PR1, and advance to PR2 (staged -> main). The process should be idempotent / resumable.

#### Actual Behavior

After PR1 #491 (external-review-test-fixes-20260530 -> staged-b329b49acf0d-1780175275) failed on the 'Script Tests' required check, I pushed a fix (the push itself succeeded via merge-to-main's pre-push hooks, updating #491's head). But neither a fresh re-run nor --resume can advance:

    $ .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh
    ERROR: non-draft PR already exists for branch external-review-test-fixes-20260530: .../pull/491

    $ .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh --resume
    ERROR: non-draft PR already exists for branch external-review-test-fixes-20260530: .../pull/491

Both paths unconditionally attempt to CREATE PR1 and abort on the existing-PR guard. There is no code path to (a) detect+reuse the existing open PR1, or (b) resume forward into the PR1-wait / PR1-merge / PR2 steps. Net: a transient PR1 CI failure wedges the branch — the fix is pushed and CI is green, but the tool cannot carry it forward. The only escapes are manual gh operations (merge or close PR1) which the workflow's own rules (rule:no-direct-gh-pr / rule:no-force-merge) discourage.

### 3. Action History

1. merge-to-main on fresh branch -> created staged ref + PR1 #491; wait-for-pr reported 'Script Tests' failed -> 'PR1 reached terminal failure state'.
2. Fixed the failing test (SIGPIPE-safe here-strings), committed, re-ran merge-to-main -> pushed fix (pre-push passed) then errored 'non-draft PR already exists'.
3. merge-to-main --resume -> same 'non-draft PR already exists' error.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

Same script family as 8cc6-4db3-717b-4274 (wait-for-pr SKIPPED-checks timeout) but a DISTINCT failure mode (idempotency / resume-after-PR1-failure, not the wait logic). Suggested fix direction: when an open non-draft PR1 already exists for the branch->staged-base, reuse it (re-wait on its checks) rather than erroring; and give --resume a resume point at PR1-wait / PR1-merge / PR2.

### 6. Logs

Live example: PR #491 OPEN, head 4256289944, base staged-b329b49acf0d-1780175275; CI re-running green after the fix; branch cannot advance via merge-to-main.

comments.body:
Second occurrence observed 2026-05-30 (variant: --resume creates DUPLICATE PR rather than erroring).

Repro path:
1. ran .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh on branch fix-g2-and-pr482-nits → created staged-6fc8b2284d4e-1780175083 + PR #490. Exit 0. Auto-merge pending on PR #490 (CI checks running).
2. While #490 was still pending, ran .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh --resume → created staged-6fc8b2284d4e-1780176147 + PR #492 (different timestamp suffix, same source branch, same diff). Exit 0.

Outcome: two open PR1s referencing the same source branch, each pointing at a different staged-* ref. Distinct from the originally-filed symptom where both invocations error "non-draft PR already exists" — here --resume bypassed the existing-PR guard entirely, possibly because of a stale or missing checkpoint file.

Hypothesis: there are TWO related defects (or one with two manifestations):
  (a) the existing-PR guard fires when checkpoint state EXISTS (gives "already exists" error) — the originally-filed symptom on PR #491
  (b) when checkpoint state does NOT exist (e.g., never written, or cleaned up between runs), the script falls through to fresh-PR-creation and produces a duplicate — the new symptom on PR #490/#492

Workaround applied: closed PR #492 via gh + deleted its staged ref.

Suggested fix scope expansion: detect existing open PR1 for the same source branch BEFORE attempting staged-ref creation, independent of checkpoint state. The check should be authoritative from gh API state, not from local checkpoint.
